reason: The broad hypothesis combines distinct outcomes and race-comparison populations whose estimated effects and inferences differ materially.
parent_hypothesis: Police stops and searches are racially biased.
dimensions: Primary outcome: search rate versus contraband hit rate
Race comparison: black versus white versus all known or unknown-inclusive categories

hypotheses.hypothesis: Among all recorded stops, Black subjects have a higher search rate than White subjects.
hypotheses.rationale: Search rate and contraband hit rate are distinct outcomes, and the multiverse results show substantial changes when the outcome is changed. The black-versus-white comparison is fixed because changing the race-comparison set also materially changes the estimated effect and inference. The claim is limited to an observable difference and does not assert a causal mechanism.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Among searched stops in all recorded stops, Black subjects have a higher rate of any contraband hit than White subjects.
hypotheses.rationale: Contraband hit rate is a different outcome from search rate and must be tested among searched stops rather than pooled with the decision to search. A specific hit definition is required because any-, drug-, and weapon-related hits produce materially different estimates. The direction follows the parent’s implied bias claim while remaining an observational comparison.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Among all recorded stops, search rates differ across the known race categories.
hypotheses.rationale: The all-known-races comparison is not interchangeable with the Black-versus-White contrast: the multiverse shows large effect changes and inference flips between these comparison sets. Because an omnibus comparison does not specify a single direction across categories, a non-directional differences claim is appropriate.
